transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-14
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Acme Dir Infra), Samantha Lee (Acme Compliance), Tom Alvarez (Acme Platform)

Auto-generated Summary (optional):
Acme is evaluating Redwood for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment in a regulated environment. Primary concerns: offline updates, signed binaries, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/ISO evidence, latency targets, hardware constraints (NVIDIA A100 vs rack-level inference), and upgrade/rollback processes. Team agreed to share security artifacts and scope a POC focusing on throughput and security controls.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya, I'm the account exec. We also have Liam from our SE team; how's everybody doing?
[00:07] Raj (Acme): Good, thanks. Ready to dig in, we have a tight window so we'll try to be efficient.
[00:11] Samantha (Acme): Hi, thanks. I'll jump in on compliance questions.
[00:15] Liam (Redwood SE): Great, quick agenda from our side — understand your constraints, security reqs, hardware footprint, and then talk through update and validation flows for air-gapped installs.
[00:23] Tom (Acme): That sounds right. We're particularly interested in offline updates and how Redwood handles model updates when there's no outbound network.
[00:30] Maya: Perfect. Maybe Raj can kick off with current stack and why you're looking at an on-prem solution?
[00:35] Raj: Sure. We're in regulated industrial controls, data residency and source-of-truth logs must never leave our network. We run a mix of k8s clusters internal, some VMs, and we have a constrained change window — quarterly patch cycles. We need an inference platform that can operate fully air-gapped and accept updates via approved media, or a bastion with controlled egress.
[00:56] Samantha: To add, we require audit trails, SSO via SAML, RBAC, and integration with our HSM for key material. SOC2 and ISO 27001 evidence is table stakes.
[01:08] Liam: Understood. On the HSM/KMS piece — we have an on-prem private deployment option that supports KMS integration and can be configured to use customer-managed HSMs, with keys never leaving the device. For air-gapped environments we support signed artifacts and offline package ingestion.
[01:26] Tom: When you say signed artifacts, do you mean model files and runtime images? How do you verify signature chains without internet?
[01:33] Liam: Good question. The approach is: Redwood produces signed bundles — binaries + model weights — signed with our code-signing certificate. For offline installs, we can provide the public cert and verification tooling so Acme can run signature verification locally. The signing chain and certificate verification don't require outbound access if you embed the root cert in your trust store.
[01:51] Samantha: That helps, but audit wants rotation proofs and ability to verify signer identity historically — like who signed what and when. Can you provide immutable audit logs that can be exported to our SIEM?
[02:03] Maya: Yes — we can provide audit logs and a documented log export format. For Private deployments we can ship an audit-forwarder, or deliver logs as part of the offline package for ingestion to customer SIEM. We'll include the log schema in the security docs.
[02:16] Raj: Another constraints is hardware. Our datacenter has a mix — a few racks with H100s but most inference capacity will be on older A30/A10 GPUs. Latency SLOs are 150-200ms for short prompts and batch throughput targets of ~150 tokens/s across a pool. How flexible is Redwood about quantized models and running on lower-memory cards?
[02:40] Liam: We do model compression and quantization recommendations per workload. For on-prem you can pin quantized variants; our runtime supports int8 paths and memory-savers. There is a tradeoff between latency and quality. We can run a benchmark on your hardware — we'll need sample prompts and model choices.
[02:55] Tom: We have a custom model family and also use open weights. Are you able to serve customer-provided models in the air-gapped install?
[03:02] Liam: Yes. We support onboarding customer models. For air-gapped we can accept the model bundle, verify signatures, and onboard it into the runtime. You can also compile optimized kernels ahead of time. Note: for some kernel-level optimizations we may need to generate platform-specific binaries; these would be built in our secure build environment and delivered as signed artifacts.
[03:23] Samantha: On the legal side, deployments must have a clear SLA for security patches. We need a vulnerability and patch cadence — how quickly do you push critical fixes?
[03:33] Maya: For Private customers we offer a patch cadence and emergency hot-fixes. We can commit to an SLA for critical security patches with a hotfix path; in air-gapped scenarios we produce a signed hotfix bundle and you apply it during your maintenance window. We will document the process and required approvals.
[03:48] Raj: How do you handle telemetry? We can't allow outbound telemetry.
[03:52] Liam: Telemetry is optional. For Private/offline installs we can disable phone-home and we provide offline metrics export. You can run Prometheus/Grafana on-prem and we provide exporters.
[04:02] Tom: What about model drift and quality monitoring? We rely on outputs being auditable and the ability to run regression tests before swapping models in production.
[04:11] Liam: We have a rollout system — canary/A-B and automatic fallback. In an air-gapped POC we'll replicate that logic locally: you can do staged rollouts and run evaluation suites. We'll work with you to define prompts and evaluation metrics so the POC includes quality checks.
[04:29] Samantha: We also need to understand data at rest encryption — are model caches or KV caches encrypted?
[04:36] Liam: Yes, disk-level encryption and optional runtime encryption for KV caches. Keys are stored in your HSM / KMS. We can provide architecture diagrams showing where data is resident and the boundaries.
[04:46] Raj: There's also procurement constraints — any hardware we order must arrive and be validated before we start. Can Redwood provide a minimum hardware spec and a validated list of cards and drivers?
[04:55] Maya: Absolutely. We'll share a validated hardware matrix and recommended AMI/container images. For on-prem we list supported GPUs, required CUDA/driver versions, and recommended NVLink/PCI topology.
[05:06] Tom: How much of the runtime is open vs closed? Our security team is more comfortable if key parts are auditable.
[05:11] Liam: The runtime core is a compiled binary — we provide a detailed architecture review and can enable third-party audits under NDA. Some components (helpers, exporters) are open-source. For high-security customers we offer source review agreements.
[05:24] Raj: What about upgrade rollback? If a new model or runtime causes issues, can we revert and how fast?
[05:30] Liam: We support version pinning and immediate rollback to a prior signed bundle. The rollback process is offline — you reapply the prior signed bundle. Our recommended POC test will validate rollback in your maintenance window.
[05:41] Samantha: For compliance, we need evidence of who applied updates and when. Does the agent produce signing events with user identity?
[05:47] Maya: Yes — the install/upgrade tooling records the user and the operator identity; we can integrate with your SSO/IDP so actions are attributed. Audit artifacts can be exported.
[05:56] Raj: Deployment topology — we want redundancy across two availability rooms in our datacenter, and an automatic failover. Does the private runtime support multi-zone replication?
[06:05] Liam: Yes, for on-prem we support clustered deployments with replication and leader election. The specifics depend on whether you're using k8s or bare-metal orchestration; we can advise and provide manifests or systemd unit examples.
[06:18] Tom: A practical question: if we accept updates via physical media, what's the recommended validation flow?
[06:23] Liam: Flow we typically recommend: 1) Redwood provides signed bundle + checksum, 2) Customer verifies signature and checksum in a staging network, 3) Run automated regression suite, 4) Approve, then apply to prod during maintenance window. All steps logged.
[06:40] Raj: What about licensing and usage metering? We need on-prem metering for billing and internal chargebacks.
[06:46] Maya: We have usage collectors that run locally and produce metering reports. For air-gapped installs we produce signed usage reports that you can upload to our portal when you have a maintenance window with limited egress, or we can bill on reserved capacity.
[06:59] Tom: Any known limitations with older GPUs like A10? Memory limits?
[07:04] Liam: On A10s you'll need smaller batch sizes and may prefer quantized models. We can give configuration profiles. We'll include those in the docs.
[07:12] Samantha: Also want to confirm—do you support an HSM-backed key for model decryption? Some vendors require keys in cloud KMS which we can't allow.
[07:20] Liam: We support customer-managed HSMs and the runtime can decrypt with keys that never leave the HSM. We can do envelope encryption where the HSM unwraps keys locally.
[07:30] Raj: Okay, timeline: we have an internal steering committee the week of 3/22; we'd like a POC scope before that. Is it realistic to have a POC in April?
[07:38] Maya: Yes — if we get the hardware inventory and signed NDA plus security questionnaire this week, we can scope and start the POC planning. Typical POC length is 4-6 weeks.
[07:47] Tom: Cost: what should we budget for a private on-prem license + support?
[07:52] Maya: I'll send a pricing template — for Dedicated/Private there are platform license fees + optional support tiers. For air-gapped enterprise contracts we usually do a term license with annual support. I'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up.
[08:02] Samantha: Please include details about the SLAs for vulnerability disclosure and patch delivery in the pricing doc.
[08:08] Maya: Will do.
[08:10] Liam: One more technical note — if you plan to use custom kernels or compile optimized code, we'll need a representative build machine spec so we can pre-build artifacts for you and sign them.
[08:21] Raj: That makes sense. We'll share the build spec.
[08:24] [Quick crosstalk about calendar slots and who will own the POC]
[08:28] Maya: Let's recap action items and next steps.
[08:31] Maya: Action items — I'll send SOC2/ISO docs, hardware matrix, and pricing. Liam will draft the POC test plan. Tom will provide hardware inventory and patch windows. Samantha will send compliance checklist items.
[08:46] Samantha: One question on evidence — can you provide sample audit logs and a mapping to our control framework?
[08:52] Liam: Yes, we'll include sample logs and a mapping doc.
[08:55] Raj: Anything else?
[08:57] Tom: No, that's all from me.
[09:00] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the doc bundle by Tuesday and propose POC dates.
[09:06] Samantha: Thanks, bye.
[09:08] Raj: Thanks, bye.

Meeting close.
